name: Simplify
definition: Complexity is the enemy of scale, speed, and customer experience. Leaders are fanatical about simplifying what they touch.

rows.situation: When the answer is another option or another setting
rows.under: Adds the option. Every request becomes a toggle.
rows.justRight: Finds the one behavior that serves most cases and removes the need for the choice.
rows.over: Refuses an option that a large group of customers genuinely needs, in the name of simplicity.

rows.under: Learns to live with it and passes it on intact.
rows.justRight: Takes a piece out each time you touch it. Leaves it simpler than you found it.
rows.over: Rewrites it from scratch and spends a year reproducing behavior that already worked.

rows.situation: When you explain the work to someone outside it
rows.under: Uses the jargon and the diagram with 40 boxes.
rows.justRight: Explains it in plain words in a minute. If you cannot, you do not understand it yet.
rows.over: Simplifies until the explanation is no longer true, and people plan against a picture that is wrong.

rows.situation: When a process has grown approvals
rows.under: Adds one more approval after the last mistake.
rows.justRight: Asks what each approval catches, and removes the ones that catch nothing.
rows.over: Strips out controls that exist because something expensive went wrong.

rows.situation: When three tools do nearly the same thing
rows.under: Adds a fourth for the case none of them cover.
rows.justRight: Picks one, moves everyone onto it, and turns the others off.
rows.over: Forces one tool onto a team whose work genuinely does not fit it.

rows.situation: When the simple option is more work to build
rows.under: Ships the complicated thing because it was faster to write.
rows.justRight: Pays the build cost once so that everyone downstream pays nothing.
rows.over: Polishes the internal elegance of something no customer will ever touch.
